title: Tondo
capsule: Tondo was the dominant polity of Manila Bay's northern shore, first documented in the Laguna Copperplate Inscription of 900 CE as 'Tundun,' attesting trade links with the Mataram kingdom of Java. By the late pre-colonial period it was a feudal bayan led by a lakan (paramount ruler) who monopolized the redistribution of Chinese trade goods throughout the archipelago; Lakandula, ruling at Spanish arrival (1570–71), exploited arriving junks by seizing sails and rudders until duties were paid. Spain's conquest of Manila in 1571 and the suppression of the Tondo Conspiracy in 1589 ended the lakandula's political power, though Tondo survived as a Manila district. Its population at Spanish contact has been estimated at approximately 43,000.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Tondo's urban core is well-located, but the extent of its tribute network and the boundaries it controlled across the Manila Bay region are uncertain and likely fluctuated considerably.
